arc-setup: Correct for subshell in arc-ureadahead arc-ureadahead attempts to exit early if its pack file is successfully read by ureadahead. When the script was migrated to use logger, the commands were moved into a compound group. Because the compound group is piped to logger, it is run in a subshell, so the exit doesn't have any effect on the parent shell. This means that the fallback arc-setup command is always run. The commands in the group always remove the packfile if it isn't valid, so instead of assuming that an early exit happens, we can just check for the pack file before running arc-setup. If it's still there, it must have been valid; if not, we need to run the fallback. BUG=chromium:930144 TEST=arc-setup --mode=read-ahead isn't run when pack file exists Change-Id: Ia21c4f45f3ba0a755b50aac9ddcda7a18ef98718 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1460341 Commit-Ready: Benjamin Gordon <bmgordon@chromium.org> Tested-by: Benjamin Gordon <bmgordon@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org>

ntfs3g: Allow non-root block device mounts when using external fuse. ntfs3g disallows non-root users (with ntfs3g suid root) from mounting block devices when built with the system libfuse. This is because the bundled libfuse has additional code to drop and restore root using setresuid() for improved security. However, ntfs3g is NOT suid-root in Chrome OS, but rather run with CAP_SYS_ADMIN by cros-disks. This causes the privilege dropping code to become a no-op because now both uid and euid are non-root. With this change, ntfs3g can be switch to using external fuse, which allows for a small disk sapce saving, and the ability to run fully unprivileged (without CAP_SYS_ADMIN). BUG=chromium:866377 TEST=platform_CrosDisksFilesystem autotest Change-Id: I5d71187d9b1ab46c33e6ad3714b42768e30ab1aa Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1454446 Commit-Ready: Anand Mistry <amistry@chromium.org> Tested-by: Anand Mistry <amistry@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Ben Chan <benchan@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org>
